injuries.notes: McLaughlin got limited opportunities early in his career, but he's played in 16 or 17 contests each of the past five years, the last three of which have been with the Bucs. He was incredibly accurate in making 94 percent of his FG attempts over his first two seasons with the club, and though that rate dropped a bit to 84 percent last year, McLaughlin also hit a career-high 11 field goals from 50-plus yards (on 12 attempts). He'll be in the final year of the three-year contract he inked in 2024, which could give McLaughlin additional incentive to make a big impact with his leg.

injuries.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuries.headline: Gainwell is one of three running backs on Tampa Bay's 53-man roster, along with Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker (undisclosed), the latter of whom didn't practice Wednesday, per Greg Auman of Fox Sports.
injuries.notes: Gainwell signed a two-year, $14 million contract with the Buccaneers in March after leading the Steelers with 73 catches in the 2025 regular season. He's likely to fill a change-of-pace role while playing primarily in passing situations, much like Rachaad White did for the past couple seasons in a Buccaneers backfield that's expected to be led by Irving as long as the latter stays healthy. Tucker could be a thorn in the side of both Gainwell and Irving from a fantasy perspective if Tucker reprises his red-zone role from 2025, which helped him punch in a team-high seven rushing touchdowns.

injuries.name: Bucky Irving
injuries.headline: Irving is set to lead a Buccaneers backfield that also includes Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker (undisclosed), the latter of whom didn't practice Wednesday, per Greg Auman of Fox Sports.
injuries.notes: Irving figures to get most of the rushing opportunities in Tampa Bay's backfield, though Gainwell is likely to play in passing situations after leading the Steelers with 73 catches in the 2025 regular season and subsequently signing a two-year, $14 million contract with the Buccaneers in March. Tucker was used frequently in the red zone last season, leading the Buccaneers with seven rushing touchdowns. Irving saw his rushing touchdown total dip to one in 10 games during his injury-plagued 2025 campaign after scoring eight regular-season rushing touchdowns as a rookie. Despite the competition for touches, Irving maintains the highest ceiling in Tampa Bay's backfield given his success in 2024.

injuries.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuries.headline: Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht praised Godwin on Monday for his consistency and veteran leadership, Brianna Dix of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: "I would be remiss if I did not mention [Godwin] for all he has done for this organization and talk about being a consistent, steady, Mr. Clutch player, that is him and he looks very, very good out there right now," Licht relayed Monday. For the first time in his NFL career, Godwin enters the season out of the shadows of Mike Evans (groin), who signed a three-year contract with the 49ers in March. Godwin logged 1,000-plus yard seasons four times from 2019 to 2023, and he was the league leader in receptions before dislocating his ankle in Week 7 of the 2024 season. He was limited to nine regular-season games last year due to a fibula injury, but Godwin is fully healthy entering the 2026 campaign and will serve as a go-to target in the passing game for quarterback Baker Mayfield. Godwin could operate in an elevated role early in the season depending on the statuses of Emeka Egbuka (toe) and Jalen McMillan (knee) for Week 1 against the Bengals on Sunday, Sept. 13.

injuries.name: Billy Schrauth
injuries.headline: Schrauth (knee) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: The rookie fifth-rounder sprained his knee in early August and was unable to participate in the preseason. The reserve offensive lineman is now back in action and healthy for the regular season. Schrauth is set to be a reserve option at guard in case Ben Bredeson or Luke Goedeke must miss time during the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Keionte Scott
injuries.headline: Scott (knee) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: Scott suffered a knee injury in last Friday's preseason finale against the Jaguars. The rookie fourth-rounder has recovered from the issue and is all set to suit up for practice. Scott is set to be one of the primary backups for the Buccaneers' secondary throughout the 2026 regular season.

injuries.name: Mohamed Kamara
injuries.headline: Kamara (knee) reverted to the Buccaneers' injured reserve list Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.notes: Kamara suffered a sprained left knee in the Buccaneers' preseason finale against the Jaguars last Friday. The linebacker was promptly waived with an injury designation and cleared waivers. Kamara will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on IR unless he is waived with an injury settlement.

injuries.name: David Sills V
injuries.headline: Sills (undisclosed) was placed on injured reserve by the Buccaneers on Sunday with a designation to return, Scott Smith of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Sills appears to have picked up an undisclosed injury at some point during the preseason. The wide receiver played in one of the team's preseason contests, reeling in one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Sills will now be forced to miss at least four contests while on IR, and the earliest he can return to action is Week 5 against the Cowboys on Oct. 8.

injuries.name: Jalon Daniels
injuries.headline: Daniels is moving forward as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback behind Baker Mayfield after impressing throughout training camp, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: After entering camp as an undrafted rookie in a crowded quarterback room, Daniels appears to have climbed into the No. 2 role behind Mayfield. The decision gives him clear roster security and places him next in line if Tampa Bay needs a backup to step into game action. Daniels won the job after a strong preseason during which he completed 27 of 44 passes for 239 yards and a touchdown without being picked off.

injuries.name: Tez Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson secured one of three targets for nine yards in the Buccaneers' 19-0 preseason loss to the Jaguars on Friday.
injuries.notes: Johnson recorded his one catch on his initial target of the night, which came with 5:47 remaining in the first quarter on the Buccaneers' second possession. Friday's action was the first of the preseason for the 2025 seventh-round pick, who'd missed the first two exhibitions due to an Aug. 4 groin strain. Johnson outperformed his draft slotting as a rookie with a 28-322-5 line over 16 regular-season games a year ago, and he should have a good chance of reprising a depth receiver role to open the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Deshawn McKnight
injuries.headline: The Buccaneers placed McKnight (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: McKnight suffered a hamstring injury in Saturday night's preseason game against the Chiefs. The rookie defensive lineman will now miss the entirety of the 2026 regular season unless he is waived with an injury settlement. The Buccaneers signed rookie wide receiver Matthew Henry in a corresponding move.

injuries.name: Tristan Wirfs
injuries.headline: Wirfs (hamstring) practiced in full-team drills Tuesday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: Wirfs looks to be ready for the season after a hamstring injury early in camp kept him sidelined for a spell. He returned in limited fashion last week and is now progressing to full-team work and one-on-ones against starters.

injuries.name: Zyon McCollum
injuries.headline: McCollum (groin) practiced Thursday and might even see some snaps in Saturday's preseason game against the Chiefs, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: The cornerback had missed the previous week of practice sessions and was not expected to suit up for Week 2 of the preseason. While there's still a chance McCollum sits against Kansas City, he at least appears to be healthy again. McCollum started all 13 regular-season games he played during the 2025 campaign and is projected to start again in 2026.

injuries.name: Vita Vea
injuries.headline: Vea (back) and the Buccaneers reached an agreement on a one-year, $30 million extension Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Vea, who is now under contract with the team through the 2027 season, made a trade request at the start of training camp, likely eyeing his AAV at the time ($17.75 million, or 19th most among interior defensive linemen). Per Jenna Laine of ESPN.com, Tampa Bay had no plans to trade Vea, though teams had checked in on the situation multiple times over the last few weeks, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. With Vea's new deal in place, the new money value of $30 million would rank fifth in AAV at his position in the NFL.

injuries.name: Cedric Gray
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out

injuries.name: Keldric Faulk
injuries.headline: Faulk (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session.
injuries.notes: Faulk had been dealing with a shoulder injury that kept him out of practice, but his full participation in Wednesday's session puts him on track to make his NFL regular-season debut Sunday against the Jets. The rookie first-rounder figures to operate in a rotational role on the Titans' defensive line behind starters Jermaine Johnson and John Franklin-Myers.

injuries.name: Mitchell Trubisky
injuries.headline: Trubisky (biceps) was not listed on the Titans' injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Trubisky was dealing with a biceps injury over the last couple of weeks of training camp, but his absence from Wednesday's injury report indicates he'll suit up for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Jets. With Will Levis no longer on the roster, Trubisky will serve as Cam Ward's backup, with Hendon Hooker on the Titans' practice squad.

injuries.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
injuries.headline: Robinson (head) is not on the Titans' Wednesday injury report.
injuries.notes: The Titans' big offseason addition at wideout will be good to go for his team debut Sunday, as Robinson carries no injury designation. Both Robinson and rookie Carnell Tate are off the injury report, signaling that Cam Ward will have his top weapons at his disposal as the team starts a new chapter under head coach Robert Saleh.

injuries.name: Carnell Tate
injuries.headline: Tate (undisclosed) is off the injury report ahead of the Titans' season opener against the Jets, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: This is a great development for Tate after he dealt with an undisclosed issue late in preseason. Tate is now on track to make his NFL debut in Week 1, when he will be a focal point of the Titans' passing game.

injuries.name: Milo Eifler
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Cam Ward
injuries.headline: New offensive coordinator Brian Daboll has worked with Ward to hone in his decision making ahead of the 2026 season, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: The first overall pick in the 2025 Draft, Ward started all 17 regular-season games as a rookie, completing 323 of 540 passes (59.8 percent) for 3,169 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions while turning 39 carries into 159 yards and two more TDs. He also fumbled 11 times, losing seven of them. The Titans added WR Carnell Tate in the first round of this year's draft and also signed WR Wan'Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70 million deal in the offseason, so Ward does have a bit more support as he enters his second pro campaign. Whether or not that helps Ward cut down on mistakes remains to be seen.

injuries.name: Tyjae Spears
injuries.headline: Spears is among the four running backs that made the Titans' initial 53-man roster.
injuries.notes: Based on preseason usage, Spears is firmly entrenched as the team's top alternative to Tony Pollard in the backfield. Spears produced 536 scrimmage yards in 2024 and 547 scrimmage yards in 2025 while filling such a role. His 838-yard rookie season in 2023 came prior to Pollard's arrival in Tennessee. Rookie fifth-round pick Nicholas Singleton didn't show anything during preseason action that would indicate he's an immediate threat to Spears' role, while Julius Chestnut is likely ticketed for a role on special teams.

injuries.name: Tony Pollard
injuries.headline: Pollard is set to lead a group of four running backs that made the Titans' initial 53-man roster.
injuries.notes: Tennessee also kept Tyjae Spears, rookie fifth-round pick Nicholas Singleton and Julius Chestnut on the 53-man roster. The decision to roster four running backs, coupled with second-year QB Cam Ward's struggles in the preseason, could indicate a desire to implement a run-heavy approach from new OC Brian Daboll. Pollard has topped 1,000 scrimmage yards in five consecutive regular seasons, the last two of which came with the Titans, and he sits atop the RB depth chart heading into the regular season, with Spears poised to reprise his change-of-pace role.

injuries.name: Calvin Ridley
injuries.headline: Ridley is among the five wide receivers on the Titans' initial 53-man roster.
injuries.notes: Tennessee heads into the season with Carnell Tate (undisclosed), Wan'Dale Robinson (head), Ridley, Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor at wide receiver. Of those five players, only Robinson and Ridley have more than one year of NFL experience. Ridley was the team's No. 1 receiver in the early part of last season but finished the year with just 303 receiving yards in seven games, as he missed time due to a hamstring injury and then fractured his fibula. Having recovered from those injuries, the 31-year-old Ridley is in contention for a starting role on the outside opposite Tate, with Robinson likely to work primarily out of the slot.

injuries.name: Gunnar Helm
injuries.headline: Helm finished the preseason slate with one catch (on two targets) for 16 yards in two appearances.
injuries.notes: Helm joined the rest of the healthy starters to kick off preseason Weeks 1 and 2, logging 26 offensive snaps between the two contests. He then was rested in Saturday's exhibition finale against the Bears along with QB Cam Ward and company. A fourth-round pick in the 2025 Draft, Helm hauled in 44 of 55 targets for 357 yards and two touchdowns in 16 regular-season games as a rookie, and he'll be looking to build upon those numbers in Year 2 under new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll.

injuries.name: Kendell Brooks
injuries.headline: Brooks (undisclosed) reverted to Tennessee's injured reserve Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.notes: It's currently unclear what issue Brooks is dealing with, but he was waived/injured Sunday and subsequently cleared waivers. As such, he's been placed on season-ending IR. Brooks could still play in 2026, though, if he works out an injury settlement with the Titans.

injuries.name: Andre James
injuries.headline: The Titans placed James (undisclosed) on injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: James was operating as a depth option at center for the Titans before he sustained an undisclosed injury. The offensive lineman will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on IR unless he is waived with an injury settlement.

injuries.name: Tanoh Kpassagnon
injuries.headline: The Titans placed Kpassagnon (undisclosed) on injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Kpassagnon is suffering from an unknown issue. The defensive end will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on injured reserve unless he is waived with an injury settlement.

injuries.name: Dorian Mausi
injuries.headline: The Titans placed Mausi (undisclosed) on injured reserve Monday with a designation to return, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Mausi is dealing with an unknown injury. The linebacker will need to miss at least the first four games of the regular season on IR before he can rejoin the Titans' active roster. The second-year player out of Auburn played in all 17 regular-season games for the Titans his rookie season, logging 341 special-teams snaps and recording nine tackles (five solo).

injuries.name: Joshua Williams
injuries.headline: The Titans placed Williams (pectoral) on injured reserve Monday with a designation to return, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Williams was unable to play in the Titans' final two preseason games due to a pectoral injury he is still recovering from. The cornerback will need to miss at least the first four games of the regular season on IR before he is permitted to rejoin the active roster. With Williams out, Micah Robinson is set to be the primary backup to Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott at outside cornerback.

injuries.name: Chimere Dike
injuries.headline: Dike secured one of two targets for nine yards in the Titans' 24-15 preseason loss to the Bears on Saturday.
injuries.notes: The speedy second-year pro opened the game with the starting offense and saw both his targets from Will Levis during the Titans' second possession. Dike had one catch in each of Tennessee's three preseason games, posting a 3-28-0 line on four targets. Dike will open the season in a reserve receiver role with big-play potential after posting a 48-423-4 line across 17 regular-season games during his rookie 2025 campaign.

injuries.name: Nicholas Singleton
injuries.headline: Singleton rushed seven times for 26 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Titans' 24-15 preseason loss to the Bears on Saturday.
injuries.notes: The rookie fifth-round pick led the team in rush attempts on the night and finished second behind D'Ernest Johnson and quarterback Hendon Hooker in rushing yards. Singleton was the first Tennessee back to log a touch, gaining six yards on a reception on the second play from scrimmage and subsequently netting 18 yards on three consecutive rush attempts to kick off the Titans' second drive. Singleton finished the preseason having rushed 15 times for 57 yards alongside Saturday's 2-18-0 receiving line across two games, and he'll now wait to see if those numbers were enough to garner him the No. 3 running back role.

injuries.name: Joey Slye
injuries.headline: Slye converted all four of his field-goal attempts and made his only PAT try in Sunday's 19-16 preseason win over the Seahawks.
injuries.notes: Slye has been locked in this preseason. He hit all four of his field-goal attempts in the preseason opener against San Francisco, with a long of 58 yards, and Slye added another 4-for-4 performance Sunday. Slye was true from 55, 33, 40 and 43 yards against the Seahawks. The big-legged kicker is thriving in the low-pressure environment of the preseason, but Slye has had accuracy issues creep up during the past three regular seasons, converting 80 percent or fewer of his field-goal attempts in each of those campaigns.

injuries.name: Jaylen Harrell
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Jaren Kanak
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Elic Ayomanor
injuries.headline: Ayomanor (shoulder) is practicing Friday, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Ayomanor exited Thursday's practice early due to an issue with his left shoulder, but he apparently dodged a serious injury. The second-year wideout is competing for slotting in Tennessee's wideout pecking order, so it's important that he didn't have to miss much time.

injuries.name: Mario Goodrich III
injuries.headline: The Titans signed Goodrich to a contract Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Goodrich has spent time with the Giants, Broncos and Jets since joining the Eagles as an undrafted free agent in 2022. The cornerback also spent some time playing for the Birmingham Stallions in the UFL, but he is ready to take another crack at NFL football. Goodrich has played in four NFL regular-season games, all in 2023, when he totaled five tackles (three solo) over 67 defensive snaps and 40 special-teams snaps.

injuries.name: Marcus Harris
injuries.headline: Harris (knee) has been participating fully in training camp practices, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injuries.notes: A sixth-round selection of the Titans in the 2025 NFL Draft, Harris appeared in 14 regular-season games (five starts) last year and logged 28 tackles (18 solo), five pass defenses and one forced fumble. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in late December but is fully healthy for training camp, where he will look to solidify a starting role in the secondary for the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Jeffery Simmons
injuries.headline: Simmons (elbow) is participating at the Titans' training camp, George Walker of the Kingsport Times News reports.
injuries.notes: Simmons underwent surgery during the offseason to address an issue with his elbow, but it doesn't seem to be limiting him now that training camp has started up. He's coming off his first All-Pro season and figures to play a massive role on Tennessee's defensive line in 2026.

injuries.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuries.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Sunday's game against the Eagles, Tashan Reed reports after Commanders coach Dan Quinn's update Friday.
injuries.notes: Croskey-Merritt was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but will apparently be fine for the season opener. He's got a tough matchup on the road in Philadelphia, and he'll will be sharing snaps with Rachaad White in some fashion, regardless of health/durability considerations.

injuries.name: Odafe Oweh
injuries.headline: Oweh (calf) was a limited participant at the Commanders' practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Oweh has been limited at back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from a calf injury he suffered in mid-August. The linebacker will have one more chance to log a full session Friday before the team's begins the regular season on the road in Philadelphia on Sunday.

injuries.name: K'Lavon Chaisson
injuries.headline: Chaisson (knee) was a limited participant at the Commanders' practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Chaisson has logged back-to-back limited sessions to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury he sustained during Washington's joint practice with Miami in early August. The 27-year-old will have one last chance to log a full practice Friday before Sunday's regular-season opener against the Eagles on the road.

injuries.name: Daron Payne
injuries.headline: Payne (knee) was a limited participant at the Commanders' practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Payne was added to the injury report Thursday after he opened the week as a full participant Wednesday. The defensive tackle is dealing with an apparent knee injury, and he will have one more chance to log a full practice Friday before the team takes on the Eagles in Week 1 on Sunday.

injuries.name: Jordan Magee
injuries.headline: Magee (chest) practiced in full Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Barring a setback, Magee is on track to suit up for Week 1 versus the Eagles. The 25-year-old most recently appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Commanders during the 2025 campaign, amassing 54 total tackles and one passes defended.

injuries.name: Tim Settle
injuries.headline: Settle (calf) is not listed on Wednesday's injury report.
injuries.notes: Settle's omission from the injury report nearly confirms he will be available for the Week 1 opener versus Philadelphia. The 29-year-old agreed to a three-year deal with the Commanders in March after accruing 15 total tackles and 1.0 sacks in 12 regular-season games for the Texans in 2025.

injuries.name: Nick Allegretti
injuries.headline: Allegretti (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Allegretti has been dealing with a calf issue since August, though his availability for Wednesday's practice suggests he will play in Week 1 versus Philadelphia, barring a setback.

injuries.name: John Bates
injuries.headline: Bates (hamstring) is not listed on the injury report for Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Despite dealing with a hamstring issue throughout the preseason, Bates is not listed on Wednesday's injury report ahead of the Week 1 meeting with the Eagles. The 28-year-old has spent his entire career with the Commanders, most recently catching 11 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown in 15 regular-season games during the 2025 campaign.

injuries.name: Ben Sinnott
injuries.headline: Sinnott (oblique) practiced in full Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Sinnott has been battling an oblique injury since the preseason. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice suggests he is cleared to suit up for the Week 1 meeting with the Eagles. The 24-year-old appeared in 16 regular-season games for the Commanders in 2025, totaling 11 catches for 114 yards and one touchdown.

injuries.name: Marcus Mariota
injuries.headline: Mariota (knee) practiced in full Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Mariota suffered a sprained MCL during the preseason, though it appears the injury is behind him heading into the Week 1 opener versus Philadelphia. The 32-year-old appeared in 11 regular-season games for the Commanders in 2025, throwing for 1,695 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions off 139-for-227 passing, adding 50 carries for 297 yards and one touchdown. Mariota currently sits at the No. 2 spot on the depth chart behind Jayden Daniels.

injuries.name: Rachaad White
injuries.headline: White (hamstring) wasn't listed on the Commanders' initial Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: White had been tending to a hamstring issue since mid-August, but his ability to avoid the practice report entirely Wednesday indicates he's put the injury behind him. Meanwhile, Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited to kick off Week 1 prep, leaving one big question mark in Washington's backfield ahead of Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

injuries.name: Athan Kaliakmanis
injuries.headline: Kaliakmanis made the Commanders' 53-man roster as the third-string quarterback, but he could be the team's backup for Week 1 against the Eagles if Marcus Mariota (knee) is not cleared to play.
injuries.notes: Mariota suffered an MCL sprain in his right knee during the Commanders' preseason game against the Dolphins on Aug. 14. The hope for the Commanders is that the veteran quarterback will be available to serve as the backup to Jayden Daniels for Week 1, but if that's not the case, then it would be Kaliakmanis who steps into the QB2 role behind Daniels. Across three preseason games, Kaliakmanis -- a seventh-round pick of the Commanders in the 2026 NFL Draft -- completed 24 of 37 passes for 294 yards with zero touchdowns and zero interceptions.

injuries.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuries.headline: Okonkwo is listed as a starting tight end on the Commanders' unofficial depth chart.
injuries.notes: After a four-year stint to begin his career in Tennessee, Okonkwo moved on to Washington via free agency this offseason, agreeing to a three-year, $27 million contract. Considering the investment made in him, it's no surprise he's listed as a first-teamer ahead of the 2026 campaign, and with lackluster competition behind him for targets in the form of John Bates (hamstring), Ben Sinnott (oblique) and Colson Yankoff, Okonkwo is poised to serve as the top TE for QB Jayden Daniels.

injuries.name: Jayden Daniels
injuries.headline: Daniels played just one possession during the Commanders' three-game preseason slate, failing to complete his only pass.
injuries.notes: Daniels suited up for preseason Week 2 at Detroit, but Washington's offense quickly went three-and-out via the aforementioned incompletion, a sack for a loss of 10 yards and an 11-yard Kaytron Allen run. Daniels otherwise remained on the sideline for the rest of exhibition season. After an outstanding rookie campaign in 2024, he endured an injury-plagued 2025, completing just 60.6 percent of his passes for 1,262 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions and rushing 58 times for 278 yards and two more TDs in seven appearances.

injuries.name: Terry McLaurin
injuries.headline: McLaurin is set to lead a group of seven wide receivers that made Washington's initial 53-man roster.
injuries.notes: McLaurin had a career-low 582 receiving yards while being limited to 10 appearances in 2025. Prior to that down year, the 2019 third-round pick out of Ohio State recorded at least 919 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL regular seasons. McLaurin and Stefon Diggs are expected to operate as the top targets for QB Jayden Daniels, with Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Treylon Burks, Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey providing depth at wide receiver.

injuries.name: Stefon Diggs
injuries.headline: Diggs is among the seven wide receivers on Washington's initial 53-man roster.
injuries.notes: The depth chart behind Diggs appears uncertain, but the veteran wide receiver seems safely locked into a starting role opposite Terry McLaurin heading into the regular season. Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Treylon Burks, Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey also made the team. Diggs has fallen short of 1,000 receiving yards only once in the past eight regular seasons.

injuries.name: Shy Tuttle
injuries.headline: The Commanders re-signed Tuttle on Monday.
injuries.notes: Tuttle was part of the Commanders' final roster cuts Sunday, but the team was able to reopen a spot for him a day later after placing offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil (triceps) on injured reserve. The 30-year-old defensive tackle previously spent time with the Titans and Commanders in 2025, appearing in 12 games while logging 15 tackles.

injuries.name: Fabian Moreau
injuries.headline: The Commanders re-signed Moreau on Monday.
injuries.notes: Moreau was part of the Commanders' final roster cuts Sunday, but the team was able to reopen a spot for him a day later after placing defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) on injured reserve. The 32-year-old cornerback had previously spent the 2025 season with the Vikings, appearing in 11 games and logging 17 tackles and two passes defensed.

injuries.name: Jer'Zhan Newton
injuries.headline: The Commanders placed Newton (pectoral) on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.notes: Newton underwent surgery to repair a torn pectoral on Aug. 20. The defensive tackle will be required to miss the first four games of the regular season at minimum before he is eligible for activation. Newton will likely take longer to return, but has a good chance of participating in the tail end of the regular season if his recovery stays on schedule.

injuries.name: Laremy Tunsil
injuries.headline: The Commanders placed Tunsil (triceps) on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.notes: Tunsil is recovering from a surgery he underwent to repair a torn right triceps. The starting left tackle will need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the active roster. In all likelihood, Tunsil will be out far longer than four games, likely missing the entirety of the 2026 regular season while he recovers.

injuries.name: Deatrich Wise Jr.
injuries.headline: Wise (undisclosed) was placed on the reserve/PUP list on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Wise had been on PUP to start camp, and though he remains with the team, he will miss at least the first four games of the regular season as a result of Sunday's development The veteran defensive end missed the bulk of the 2025 season with a quadriceps injury, but it's unclear if this current issue is related.

injuries.name: Trey Amos
injuries.headline: Amos (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Sunday with a designation to return.
injuries.notes: The second-year corner will miss at least the first four games of the season for the Commanders as he works his way back from an ankle injury sustained during training camp. Amos played in 10 games as a rookie, logging 32 tackles and six pass breakups over 511 snaps.

injuries.name: Jeremy McNichols
injuries.headline: The Commanders placed McNichols (quadriceps) on injured reserve with a designation to return Sunday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: As a result of the transaction, McNichols won't be eligible to make his 2026 debut until at least Week 5 while he recovers from the quad injury, which he sustained earlier this month. Once reinstated, McNichols could have a role on special teams for the Commanders, but he'll likely be in line for limited snaps on offense if all of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (lower body), Rachaad White (hamstring) and Kaytron Allen are healthy and available out of the backfield.

injuries.name: Antonio Williams
injuries.headline: Williams didn't play in Friday's preseason loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: The third-round rookie out of Clemson has been coming on strong as training camp has progressed, and per Donna Hopkins of MASN, Williams opened some eyes in joint practices against Baltimore earlier in the week when he beat Kyle Hamilton in one-on-one drills. The fact that Williams was held out Friday along with the rest of the Commanders' key personnel could be a strong sign that he's won the No. 3 receiver job to begin the season over the likes of Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane, but he still faces an uphill battle for targets working behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs.

injuries.name: Luke McCaffrey
injuries.headline: McCaffrey caught one of three targets for 17 yards in Friday's 41-3 preseason loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: The Commanders rested all their key personnel and only managed 102 passing yards on the night on 16 completions, putting McCaffrey's line in some perspective. The third-year wideout is fighting for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, but the fact that third-round rookie Antonio Williams didn't play at all Friday could be a sign that the job has slipped away from McCaffrey.
